2609.18649.title: DyMT-ESB: Dynamic Multi-Turn Evaluation of Social Bias in User-LLM Interactions
2609.18649.paper_summary: Warning: This paper contains examples of stereotypes and social bias. LLMs are increasingly used in interactive settings by the general public, making the evaluation of model behavior in multi-turn conversational scenarios important for safety, including stereotyping-related harms. However, existing multi-turn social bias evaluations often rely on pre-specified or template-based user inputs that do not adapt to model responses and typically assume a fixed dialogue length in advance. In this paper, we study social bias dynamics in response-conditioned multi-turn interactions using a controlled evaluation protocol that generates follow-up user queries from the evolving dialogue history and allows evaluation over variable numbers of turns. Experimental results show that LLMs exhibit social bias even in coherent, response-conditioned multi-turn interactions, revealing late-emerging bias, non-monotonic bias patterns, and bias re-emergence. These results motivate evaluations that extend beyond fixed-turn, pre-scripted protocols. Our findings highlight the importance of analyzing social bias as a turn-level dynamic phenomenon.
2609.18649.paper_summary_zh: 警告：本文包含刻板印象和社會偏見的例子。大型語言模型（LLMs）在互動環境中被公眾越來越多地使用，使得在多回合對話場景中評估模型行為對於安全性變得重要，包括與刻板印象相關的傷害。然而，現有的多回合社會偏見評估通常依賴於預先指定或基於模板的用戶輸入，這些輸入不會根據模型的回應進行調整，並且通常預先假設固定的對話長度。在本文中，我們研究了在響應條件下的多回合互動中的社會偏見動態，使用一種控制評估協議，該協議根據不斷演變的對話歷史生成後續用戶查詢，並允許在可變的回合數上進行評估。實驗結果顯示，LLMs即使在連貫的響應條件下的多回合互動中也表現出社會偏見，揭示了晚現偏見、非單調偏見模式和偏見再現。這些結果促使我們進行超越固定回合和預先編寫協議的評估。我們的發現突顯了將社會偏見分析作為回合級動態現象的重要性。
